per_article_analyses.values: Truth-telling over comforting myths, skepticism of both government and media narratives, belief that understanding actual mechanisms is more important than maintaining faith in institutions, concern that overselling Fed capabilities ultimately undermines credibility.
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Wryly skeptical and gently iconoclastic. Uses humor (the Chick-fil-A observation) and irony to puncture conventional wisdom while maintaining respectful tone toward Fed officials, suggesting disappointment in widespread misunderstanding rather than anger at deception.

per_article_analyses.title: Update On Interest Rates: Is The Federal Reserve Shooting Blanks? (2024-10-07)
per_article_analyses.concerns: The fundamental disconnect between Federal Reserve rate policy and actual market behavior, questioning whether the Fed's power to influence the economy is real or merely an illusion based on market faith.
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Data-driven contrarian analysis that systematically dismantles accepted wisdom by showing concrete market evidence that contradicts the Fed's supposed influence
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Uses vivid metaphors ('shooting blanks,' 'confidence game,' 'illusion'), presents stark statistical contrasts (92% correlation vs 34% correlation), and employs visual data presentations to highlight contradictions
per_article_analyses.values: Skepticism toward institutional authority, preference for market truth over policy theater, belief that economic reality should trump political/institutional narratives
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Cool analytical skepticism with undertones of concern - methodically building a case that a fundamental assumption about economic policy may be wrong

per_article_analyses.title: Prediction Markets: How Reliable Are They Really? (Part 1) (2024-10-23)
per_article_analyses.concerns: Whether prediction markets represent a genuine improvement over traditional polling for forecasting political outcomes, and what their limitations and failure modes might be as they scale rapidly.
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Balanced analytical exploration that explains the theoretical foundation (Wisdom of Crowds, EMH) while systematically identifying potential weaknesses and risks
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Uses historical analogies (Dewey defeats Truman), draws parallels between financial theory and political forecasting, presents both promise and peril through data visualization
per_article_analyses.values: Intellectual honesty about new technologies, preference for market mechanisms over traditional institutions, but wariness about over-promising on untested systems
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Cautiously optimistic but intellectually rigorous - interested in the innovation but determined to stress-test the assumptions before embracing it

per_article_analyses.title: Is Price Gouging Real? Who's Doing It? Is It Driving Inflation? (2024-11-14)
per_article_analyses.concerns: Testing the popular political narrative of 'corporate greed' driving inflation against actual profit margin data to determine where real price gouging might be occurring.
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Methodical data-driven investigation that systematically examines different industry sectors using a clear analytical framework (profit margin expansion during price increases)
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Contrasts popular political narratives with hard data, uses sector-by-sector analysis to build credibility before revealing surprising conclusions about banking
per_article_analyses.values: Empirical truth over political convenience, willingness to challenge both popular narratives and defend unpopular industries when data supports it
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Dispassionate investigative analysis that builds to a 'gotcha' moment - finding the real culprit (banks) where few were looking

per_article_analyses.title: China's Economic Problem Isn't Just 'Japanification' – It May Be Worse (2025-02-06)
per_article_analyses.concerns: China faces not just Japanese-style stagnation but a more dangerous combination of deflation and currency devaluation that creates a policy trap with no clear escape.
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Historical comparison analysis that builds credibility through detailed Japan parallels before revealing the crucial difference that makes China's situation potentially more perilous
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Uses extensive historical precedent (Japan, FDR's dollar devaluation) to establish patterns, then dramatically reveals how China breaks the pattern in an ominous way
per_article_analyses.values: Rigorous historical analysis, concern for economic stability, appreciation for the complexity of monetary policy tools and their limitations
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Growing concern and alarm - starts with academic comparison but builds to warning about systemic instability and potential economic disorder

per_article_analyses.title: China's Economic Crisis Is Tracking Japan's Downturn In The 1990's (2025-02-15)
per_article_analyses.concerns: Documenting the systematic parallels between China's current economic crisis and Japan's 1990s stagnation across multiple indicators, with implications for geopolitical stability.
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Comprehensive comparative analysis using multiple data streams (stocks, housing, debt, unemployment) to build an overwhelming case for the Japan parallel
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Methodical sector-by-sector comparison with extensive data visualization, uses projection charts to suggest future trajectories, builds cumulative weight of evidence
per_article_analyses.values: Thorough empirical analysis, attention to socio-political implications beyond pure economics, appreciation for long-term demographic and generational consequences
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Soberly concerned documentation - clinical in analysis but increasingly grave in implications, particularly regarding youth unemployment and social stability

per_article_analyses.title: Tariffs: First, Consider The Certainties
per_article_analyses.concerns: The need to establish factual ground truth about tariffs before engaging with heated political rhetoric. Concerned with distinguishing between what is actually known versus highly disputed about tariff policy, and providing historical context for current debates.
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Methodical historical survey combined with framework-setting analysis. Builds the case by establishing 'Known Knowns' versus 'Known Unknowns,' using extensive historical documentation to show tariffs as central to American policy for 150+ years before becoming 'fiscally irrelevant.'
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Heavy use of historical data and charts to establish credibility. Creates analytical frameworks (Certainties vs Uncertainties). Uses concrete statistics and dates to anchor abstract policy debates. Appeals to the complexity of the issue to resist oversimplification.
per_article_analyses.values: Intellectual rigor over political positioning. Values historical perspective and data-driven analysis. Believes in the importance of understanding asymmetric trade relationships and the strategic use of trade policy as both economic and geopolitical tool.
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Measured and professorial, with undertones of frustration at shallow media coverage. Presents himself as reluctant expert pulled into the fray. Tone is cautious and systematic rather than advocating for any particular position.

per_article_analyses.title: Tariff Uncertainties – Part 2: The Link To Inflation
per_article_analyses.concerns: Whether tariffs actually cause inflation, examining the logical case for both sides and the weakness of available evidence. Fundamentally concerned with the gap between theoretical models and messy economic reality.
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Contrarian analysis that challenges seemingly obvious conclusions. Presents two competing theoretical frameworks (Construct 1 vs Construct 2), then systematically examines empirical evidence from 2018-2019 tariffs and finds surprisingly weak inflationary effects.
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Uses economic data and Federal Reserve studies to challenge conventional wisdom. Employs detailed methodological critique of economic models. Creates executive summary for accessibility while maintaining analytical depth. Questions the precision of inflation metrics themselves.
per_article_analyses.values: Empirical evidence over theoretical assumptions. Skeptical of models that ignore behavioral adjustments and market responses. Values precision in economic measurement and is concerned about policy-making based on incomplete data.
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Analytically skeptical but not dismissive. Shows frustration with oversimplified economic models while maintaining scholarly tone. More confident in challenging consensus views when data supports skepticism.

per_article_analyses.title: Tariff Uncertainties, Part 3: The Bond Markets
per_article_analyses.concerns: Whether tariff announcements actually caused the massive Treasury bond market disruption, or whether the bond market's problems are deeper and more structural. Concerned with proportionality between supposed cause and dramatic effect.
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Scale-based argument that challenges causal attribution. Uses proportionality principle to argue that small tariff effects cannot logically explain massive bond market convulsions. Identifies multiple structural anomalies in Treasury markets predating tariff announcements.
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Fire/cigarette analogy to distinguish triggers from underlying causes. Extensive use of financial market data and technical indicators. Appeals to engineering concepts (linear vs nonlinear responses) to explain market behavior.
per_article_analyses.values: Proportional reasoning and logical causation. Values understanding of complex financial systems over simple political explanations. Concerned about structural stability of Treasury markets as foundation of global financial system.
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Concerned and analytical, with growing alarm about underlying structural problems in bond markets. Less interested in tariff politics than in potential financial system instability.

per_article_analyses.title: Tariff Uncertainties, Part 4: A Little Q&A (Trump, Trade, China)
per_article_analyses.concerns: Providing straightforward assessment of Trump's tariff strategy, its likely endgame, and implications for global trade relationships. Particularly focused on China as the central challenge to the current global trade system.
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Q&A format allows for direct, less hedged responses. Builds case that there is a coherent strategy behind apparent chaos, and that China represents a unique challenge requiring different approach than traditional trade partners.
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Conversational tone breaks from academic style of other pieces. Uses currency data and capital flow analysis to support arguments. References historical precedents (Marshall Plan) to contextualize current policies.
per_article_analyses.values: Fairness in global trade relationships. Believes current system is unsustainably asymmetric. Values strategic thinking over diplomatic niceties. Sees need for enforcement mechanisms in international trade.
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: More direct and less hedged than other pieces. Shows clearer policy preferences while maintaining analytical stance. Expresses frustration with ineffective international institutions like WTO.

per_article_analyses.title: Tariff Uncertainties, Pt 5: The Big One – Will It Cause A Recession?
per_article_analyses.concerns: Whether tariff policies will trigger an economic recession, examining four potential transmission channels and finding most concerns overblown. Fundamentally about separating psychological fears from economic reality.
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Systematic examination of four potential causal pathways from tariffs to recession, finding each insufficient. Uses real-time economic data to show continued economic strength despite tariff fears. Emphasizes behavioral evidence over sentiment surveys.
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Creates framework of four transmission channels for systematic analysis. Uses 'mango parable' to illustrate economic concepts accessibly. Contrasts what people say (sentiment surveys) with what they do (spending/investment data).
per_article_analyses.values: Behavioral evidence over reported sentiment. Values real economic indicators over forecaster predictions. Believes psychological factors are crucial but haven't yet translated into recessionary behavior.
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Cautiously optimistic and somewhat dismissive of forecaster panic. Shows confidence in economic resilience while acknowledging uncertainty as the main risk factor.

per_article_analyses.title: The False Promises Of Economic Forecasting (Newly Exposed By The 'Tariff Whiplash')
per_article_analyses.concerns: The fundamental unreliability and volatility of professional economic forecasts as predictive tools, exposed through the dramatic reversals in recession predictions during the 2025 'tariff shock' period
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Data-driven empirical takedown using statistical analysis and historical examples to systematically demolish the credibility of economic forecasting, marshaling evidence from multiple prestigious sources (WSJ surveys, Fed models, major banks) to show consistent failure patterns
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Heavy use of statistical measures (relative standard deviation, correlation analysis), ironic juxtaposition of 'expert' predictions with reality, systematic cataloging of failed forecasts with specific percentages and timeframes, appeals to scientific measurement standards from other fields
per_article_analyses.values: Empirical rigor over institutional prestige, statistical precision, transparency in acknowledging systemic failures, preference for evidence-based analysis over expert authority
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Cool analytical demolition with undertones of frustrated exasperation at institutional incompetence, building to a call for fundamental reform

per_article_analyses.title: A Long-Overdue Reckoning For The Bureau Of Labor Statistics
per_article_analyses.concerns: The methodological breakdown and institutional decay of the BLS jobs reporting system, which produces critical economic data that moves markets and informs Federal Reserve policy despite being fundamentally flawed
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Institutional critique combining technical analysis of statistical problems (volatility, precision measures) with broader arguments about bureaucratic obsolescence and the need for technological modernization
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Statistical precision metrics (RSD calculations) compared to industrial quality standards, appeals to bipartisan expert consensus, systematic documentation of revision volatility, calls for modernization framed as inevitable technological progress
per_article_analyses.values: Statistical rigor and precision, institutional accountability, technological modernization over bureaucratic tradition, non-partisan technocratic competence
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Measured institutional criticism with underlying urgency about systemic breakdown, concluding with pragmatic calls for reform while acknowledging political complications

per_article_analyses.title: Will The Fed Cut Interest Rates? Does It Matter? Recent History Says No.
per_article_analyses.concerns: The breakdown of the traditional relationship between Federal Reserve interest rate policy and market interest rates, suggesting the Fed's primary monetary policy tool may no longer function effectively
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Historical correlation analysis demonstrating a fundamental shift in monetary policy transmission mechanisms, using statistical evidence to challenge conventional assumptions about Fed effectiveness
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Sharp statistical contrasts (90% positive correlation vs 80-90% negative correlation), historical parallels to Greenspan's 'conundrum,' automotive metaphors about broken policy levers, scale comparisons between policy targets and actual markets
per_article_analyses.values: Empirical evidence over policy orthodoxy, skepticism toward central bank effectiveness, preference for data-driven analysis of institutional performance
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Analytical concern building to institutional skepticism, with undertones of worry about fundamental breakdown in economic policy mechanisms

per_article_analyses.title: The Tariff Scorecard: Did We Miss The Apocalypse? Or Was It Just Postponed?
per_article_analyses.concerns: Reality-checking the dire predictions about tariff impacts against actual economic outcomes five months after implementation, questioning whether expert forecasts of economic catastrophe were accurate
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Systematic empirical scorecard approach, methodically examining each predicted negative outcome against actual data, building a comprehensive case that expert predictions were largely wrong
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Catalogs of apocalyptic language from experts contrasted with mundane positive data, systematic 'scorecard' format, acknowledgment of limitations and timeframe issues, ironic noting of failed predictions
per_article_analyses.values: Empirical reality over expert consensus, skepticism toward alarmist forecasting, appreciation for economic adaptability and human behavioral responses to policy changes
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Measured vindication with slight undertone of 'I told you so,' balanced by careful acknowledgment that long-term effects remain uncertain

per_article_analyses.title: The Case Against Quarterly Reporting – Part 2, The Dysfunctional Earnings Game
per_article_analyses.concerns: How quarterly earnings reporting has devolved into a manipulated game between companies and analysts that distorts market information and harms investors, using Fiserv as a case study
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Case study approach using Fiserv's dramatic stock collapse to illuminate systemic problems, combined with statistical analysis of earnings 'beats' and 'misses' to show the game's rigged nature
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Dramatic opening narrative of corporate destruction, statistical analysis of asymmetric rewards/punishments, detailed exposition of gaming techniques, appeals to principles of market fairness and transparency
per_article_analyses.values: Market transparency and fairness, investor protection, preference for 'economic reality' over financial engineering, skepticism toward institutional gaming
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Investigative exposé tone with underlying outrage at systematic market manipulation disguised as legitimate reporting

per_article_analyses.title: Make Venezuela Great Again? Pt 1: What Happened – The Rise And Fall
per_article_analyses.concerns: Understanding Venezuela's collapse through economic rather than political lens; challenging the assumption that rebuilding Venezuela should simply recreate a petrostate model under new management
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Historical-economic analysis with heavy use of quantitative data; systematic debunking of political explanations in favor of structural economic determinism; comparative analysis across time periods and against other countries
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Extensive marshaling of statistical evidence and GDP comparisons; Marx quote for intellectual authority; sports/gambling metaphors ('derivative' vs 'underlying'); ironic contrasts (wealthy quasi-colonial state vs poor quasi-colonial state); systematic periodization of decline
per_article_analyses.values: Economic fundamentalism over political explanations; skepticism toward simple solutions; emphasis on human capital and education as crucial national assets; concern for evidence-based policy rather than ideology
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Analytical concern with undertones of foreboding; presents as dispassionate economist but with clear worry about repeating mistakes; mix of scholarly detachment and implicit warning

per_article_analyses.title: Venezuela Great Again? Pt 2: The Inevitability Of A Failed Petrostate
per_article_analyses.concerns: Demonstrating that Venezuela's collapse was economically inevitable due to structural flaws in the petrostate model; warning against recreating the same system that led to failure
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Economic determinism argument built through systematic analysis of 'resource curse' mechanisms; dual-pathway causal analysis (private sector effects vs public sector effects); heavy reliance on correlation data and structural economic theory
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Prophetic opening with Pérez Alfonzo's prediction; extensive use of economic correlations and percentages; IMF and World Bank data as authoritative sources; metaphors of addiction and disease; systematic categorization of spending priorities
per_article_analyses.values: Belief in economic laws as more powerful than political will; emphasis on diversification and fiscal discipline; concern about corruption as systemic rather than moral failing; skepticism toward subsidy-based economics
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Fatalistic but intellectually satisfied tone - the satisfaction of explaining inevitability; combines scholarly analysis with implicit 'I told you so' toward those who ignored economic fundamentals

per_article_analyses.title: 'Hedge Funds' Got Clipped By Epic Fury. They Forgot To 'Hedge'?
per_article_analyses.concerns: Exposing how hedge funds have abandoned their original risk-mitigation purpose and become speculative vehicles that failed to prepare for predictable geopolitical events
per_article_analyses.argumentative_style: Contrarian takedown combining historical analysis of hedge fund evolution with forensic examination of recent failures; systematic debunking of hedge fund mystique through performance data
per_article_analyses.rhetorical_devices: Ironic title and running theme of funds forgetting to hedge; extensive market data and correlation analysis; rhetorical questions highlighting inexplicable behavior; technical financial terminology mixed with accessible explanations; metaphors of addiction and autism for institutional behavior
per_article_analyses.values: Emphasis on proper risk management over speculation; belief that human judgment should override algorithmic trading; skepticism toward financial complexity that obscures basic principles; concern for market transparency and rational preparation
per_article_analyses.emotional_register: Mixture of technical analysis and sardonic critique; intellectual superiority toward supposedly sophisticated actors who missed obvious signals; frustrated incredulity at professional incompetence
